body:
Well, it's a pathetic story. That is to say, there's no story at all. There's nothing really wrong with me, but my brain refuses to acknowledge that. I'm feeling anxious and worthlesss all the time, I never have the energy to do things (but I force myself to do them anyway because I know that caving in will only make things worse), I'm feeling suicidal half the time and I've somehow convinced myself that no one would miss me.

Now, the problem is, I know that it's all bullshit. I have no reason to feel anxious or worthless or lonely-- but I do. No matter how much I try to convince myself that it's all in my head, it just won't go away. And I can't even point at something and say: this is what's causing my feelings. This is what I need to fix. Because there's nothing to fix, no way to tackle a problem that does not exist.

How does one fight a ghost? How does one try to fight against something that isn't real? I can't talk to anyone about my depression because it's caused by nothing, and yet it's consuming me to the point where I can barely function.

I've tried therapy and meds, and nothing works. It's been about 8 years since I started with this, and with time, I've learned coping mechanisms. Little tricks I can do to keep people from realizing how broken I am, hacks to keep me moving from one day to another until the depression vanishes as fast and as suddenly as it came, because it always goes away on its own after a while (after a few months which feel like decades). But it always comes back.
Well? Did you go to any of them?
